title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page was photographed upside down (rotated 180°). After mentally rotating it, almost none of the cursive text can be read reliably. Only the symbols, the arrows and the general layout can be recovered, so what follows is a hedged reconstruction.

Context. The previous page treats a proper smooth curve f: X → S in characteristic p. It sets up the self-dual diagram linking:
- R^1f_*(O_X)^{(p)};
- H^1_DR, with its Hodge filtration;
- f_*(Ω^1_{X/S})^{(p)};
- Frobenius F, the Cartier operator C, and the conjugate filtration.

The next page is headed 'Connexions et stratifications intégrables (suite, problèmes divers)'.

What this page shows, read in the correct orientation:
- Several lines mention a morphism written 'F : X → Z' (or f : X → Z). The letter Z looks the same after a 180° rotation, so it is certainly Z. Most plausibly Z = X^{(p)}, or more generally an intermediate scheme with X^p ⊂ Z ⊂ X. This is the relative-Frobenius / height-one radicial setting that underlies the Cartier operator.
- The lines repeatedly compare X and Z. They appear to be about how objects on X (modules, connections, the de Rham complex) descend to or are computed on Z.
- There are two commutative squares. In the transcription they read as T' → T over X' → Z (or X' → X). Once rotated correctly, the arrows reverse. They become base-change squares: a morphism X → Z (labelled F or g, marked '(!!)' and '[!]') with two auxiliary schemes T, T' mapping to it.
- One square seems to compare a map over X with a map over Z. The other compares a self-map X → X (possibly absolute Frobenius, or a lift), with a question mark on the top arrow. This suggests Grothendieck was asking whether a certain arrow T' → T exists or is unique, i.e. a lifting or factorization question through Frobenius.
- A braced condition near the foot of the page has the form '{ … ∈ … , … ∈ … }'. It looks like a membership criterion, perhaps characterising which sub-objects come from Z.
- The first two lines of the image, which are the last lines of the page in reading order, are struck out.

Plausible mathematical content: preparatory remarks for Cartier descent. That is the equivalence between quasi-coherent modules on Z and O_X-modules with integrable connection of p-curvature zero, for radicial height-one morphisms X → Z. It would come with a base-change / functoriality check for squares of the displayed shape. This leads naturally into the next page on connections and stratifications. Nothing beyond this standard framework can be extracted from the image.
errors: Cannot check correctness: the text is largely illegible in the photographed orientation. The diagrams as transcribed have reversed arrows and swapped rows because of the 180° rotation.

ideas.what: Relative Frobenius F: X → X^{(p)} (written X → Z) as the setting for the Cartier operator and Cartier descent
ideas.modern_name: Cartier descent / Cartier isomorphism for a height-one radicial morphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Cartier (1957); Katz (1970, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem')
ideas.where_published: Related material in Berthelot's and Katz's work and in SGA-era seminars; Grothendieck's own exposition here is unpublished.

ideas.what: Base-change squares T' → T over X' → Z, with a questioned top arrow (existence of a factorization or lift)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly illegible and upside down. What survives (Frobenius X → Z, base-change squares, a membership condition) is consistent with standard Cartier-descent preliminaries and shows no identifiable new result.
transcription_corrections: The whole page is rotated 180°. The two struck-out lines at the top of the image are actually the last lines of the page.

In the true orientation the diagrams have reversed arrows and swapped rows. The first square reads X → Z on top with T, T' below mapping up (or with the arrows reversed accordingly), not T' → T over X' → Z.
The letter read as 'Z' is genuinely Z (it is invariant under 180° rotation). The letters read as 'T' are probably other letters seen upside down (possibly Y or ⊥) and should be marked uncertain.
The labels '(!!)' and '[!]' are attached to the lower horizontal arrow X → X and to its target in the second square.
The braced expression near the foot of the image is a two-line membership condition '{… ∈ …, … ∈ …}' and is not transcribed.
